P1-04.title: Batch-rename logic
P1-04.summary:
Branch port/P1-04 is committed with the Port-Stage trailer, and the worktree is detached. Both gates pass: `tools/parity/gen.sh --check` (26 suites up to date) and `scripts/ci.sh` (build, test with 499 passing, format).
Added `Sources/FTFoundation/BatchRename/`, with settings and types, `proposeNames`, `planBatchRename` (number, skip, block), saved-settings and preset sanitizers, and `JSRegExp`.
`JSRegExp` runs JavaScript unicode-mode regexes on `NSRegularExpression` after translating the pattern. It rewrites `$`, `.`, `\d \w \s \b`, named groups and literals so ICU's case folding matches JavaScript's.
The sanitizers are wired into `BatchRenameSanitizers.standard` in `PreferencesSanitizer.swift`, and `.passthrough` now points at it.
Goldens `batch-rename-propose` (600 cases, 2.7 MB) and `batch-rename-plan` (300 cases, 1.5 MB) both pass. A separate 322-case regex fuzz found a few differences, listed below. I used it to find them and did not commit it.
The 58 tests from `shared/batchRename.test.ts` are ported, plus the planning half of the 9 `batchRenamePlanAndRun` tests, each with its T-id. The run half is P3-08.
notes: P1-03 asks: wire sanitizeBatchRenameSettings/Presets through BatchRenameSanitizers in Sources/FTFoundation/Preferences/PreferencesSanitizer.swift
sharedFileRequests: Sources/FTFoundation/Preferences/AppState.swift: its default arguments still say `.passthrough`. That now equals `BatchRenameSanitizers.standard`, so nothing breaks, but the integrator may want to rename them to `.standard` and drop `.passthrough`.
After merging, the integrator runs `bun tools/parity-matrix/sync.ts` to pick up the T-ids cited in `Tests/FTFoundationTests/BatchRename/BatchRenameTests.swift`. I did not touch `docs/port/parity/`.
deviations: The pattern-error text after 'The pattern isn’t valid: ' is this port's own wording, not V8's or JavaScriptCore's. The goldens compare only the prefix; whether a pattern is an error matches the reference on every pattern tested.

A few regex edge cases still differ from JavaScript and are documented on `JSRegExp`. They are: a back reference to a group that took no part, which fails here but matches the empty string in JavaScript; `\P{Lu}` under the `i` flag; the captures of empty loops such as `(a*)*` and `(|a)+`; look-behinds that are not of bounded length; and a ligature such as ﬁ inside a character class also matching 'fi'.
A saved text setting cut at 255 UTF-16 units inside a surrogate pair leaves U+FFFD here, where JavaScript keeps half the pair, because a Swift String cannot hold a lone surrogate.
The reference runs on Bun's JavaScriptCore, not V8, so the goldens record JSC's regex behaviour. The two engines are not known to differ on the tested patterns, but I did not check against V8.
The golden JSON files are large (4.2 MB together).

fixes.summary:
Both findings are fixed in commit 56cb652f5cc90a7e712fae48aa1b0f0408469e83, which carries the Port-Stage: fixed-1 trailer. The branch is detached. `tools/parity/gen.sh --check` and `scripts/ci.sh` both pass (637 tests, 0 failing). Nothing was shown on screen.

1. **Failed watch leaked its stream.** In `FolderWatches.start`, the onFail closure now calls `watch.stop?()` before setting it to nil. The ProbeFail test failed before the change and passes after it; it is copied to `Tests/FTFileSystemTests/Watch/ProbeFailTests.swift`.

2. **Realpath and stream start on the main thread.** `FSEventsFolderWatcher.watchFolder` now returns a stop function immediately. It does the realpath and `FSEventStreamCreate`/`Start` in a detached task, and only the callbacks run on the main actor. A stop called before the stream has started stops it on arrival. The old synchronous body is now `openStream`. I did not add a test that measures main-thread blocking. Instead I added `stoppedBeforeTheStreamIsStartedLeavesNoStream` and changed two existing stream tests to the new return type.

One behavior difference from the reference: a folder that can't be watched (missing, say) used to give nil, so nothing was reported until the next watch() or focus retry. Because the start is now asynchronous, that case calls `onFail`, which makes the window re-read the folder once. `cannotWatchAFolderThatIsNotThere` now expects that `onFail`.

P2-02.title: Folder sizes
P2-02.summary:
The folder-size work is committed on port/P2-02 and the branch is detached. `scripts/ci.sh` passes four runs in a row (652 tests) and `tools/parity/gen.sh --check` passes. Nothing showed a window or took focus.
- C walker: `Sources/CFileTrail/foldersize.c` plus `include/ft_foldersize.h` is the original ported almost verbatim, with N-API replaced by a small C API. Walker timing is in the next line.
- Benchmark (deep tree, 200k files, release build, warm runs): the port's median was about 315-317 ms against the reference's 322-324 ms. The opt-in `FolderSizeBenchTests` ran at the deviation-free config; it is skipped unless `FILETRAIL_BENCH=1`.
- Swift in `Sources/FTFileSystem/FolderSize/`: `NativeFolderSize` (single-flight FIFO, wakes the consumer through an AsyncStream) and `FolderSizeCache`. It also holds `FolderSizeAdjust`, `FolderSizeJobs` (one job per window, utility QoS for automatic jobs, cache first, 256 finished jobs, Home Trash) and `FolderSizeWrites`. Path keys compare by exact UTF-8, because Swift string equality would merge NFC and NFD names.
- Tests: 98 added in `Tests/FTFileSystemTests/FolderSize/`, one for one with the tests.tsv rows (the cache, adjust, folder-size job and folder-size/item-size/single-flight rows). The rows for polling the active walk are marked N/A (T-e078d98d) or ported as "nothing more is delivered after a walk ends" (T-263a6e9b). `sync.ts --no-write` shows all 96 rows in scope covered (95 passing, 1 N/A).
- Golden: `tools/parity/golden/folder-size-trees.ts` is marked machine-local, so `gen.sh --check` skips it. It records the reference walker on `names`, `lighthouse`, `bench/files-300`, `bench/files-3000` and four generated trees with unreadable folders. The Swift test matches all 8 cases.
sharedFileRequests: Sources/CFileTrail/include/CFileTrail.h: I added one line, `#include "ft_foldersize.h"`, because SwiftPM treats that header as the umbrella header and the C API is invisible to Swift without it. It is already applied on this branch. Other C work packages will touch the same file, so expect a trivial merge conflict. The integrator may want to keep one include line per package.

docs/port/parity/tests.tsv and features.md were NOT committed. The integrator should run `bun tools/parity-matrix/sync.ts` after merge. Feature rows cited: F-142, F-179, F-180, F-181, F-182, F-186, F-188, F-238.
deviations: The original polls the finished folders every 200 ms. Here a worker's notification wakes the consumer at most once per 20 ms, so folders arrive in batches of whatever finished in that window. Walk results are the same.

Public API shape differs from the TypeScript. The walker is a `@MainActor` protocol `FolderSizeNative` (`getFolderSize` returns a Task, `cancelFolderSize`). `FolderSizeJobs` replaces `createFolderSizeHandlers`. `FolderSizeWrites` replaces the folder-size half of `clearResponseCaches`, `noteWriteStarting` and `noteWriteEnded` (its `forget` does nothing when both lists are empty).

Job storage is per `FolderSizeJobs` instance, not a module global as in responseCache.ts, so `jobCount` stands in for `getResponseCacheSizes().folderSizeJobs`. `FolderSizeWrites` holds its listeners weakly, where the original keeps them forever.
The opt-in benchmark test is compiled in all builds but does nothing without `FILETRAIL_BENCH=1`. It is meant for `swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing`.
Test-only: the cache tests use a different seeded generator than the TypeScript (its JS doubles lose precision), so the random sequences differ. The property checked is the same.

Test-only: Foundation's `createDirectory` and `createSymbolicLink` respell non-ASCII names, which changed symlink sizes and folder keys. The tests build trees with `mkdir`, `open` and `symlink` instead.

Test-only: ThumbnailStoreTests, which depend on short timers, failed in 3 of 4 `scripts/ci.sh` runs while my walker tests ran in parallel. I serialized the real-walk suites under one `.serialized` suite and kept the large main-actor test loads in yielding batches. After that, 4 of 4 runs passed.

The data-race-prone case (a folder that can't be opened for a reason other than EACCES/EPERM/ENOENT/ENOTDIR/ELOOP, which leaves its parent incomplete) and the out-of-memory paths are ported but have no test, because the original has none and they cannot be provoked safely.

findings.title: Log context objects: key order and key quoting differ from util.inspect({sorted:true})
findings.where: Sources/FTFileSystem/Logging/LogFormat.swift (inspect, inspectKey) vs apps/desktop/src/main/appLog.ts formatArgs (inspect options: sorted, compact, breakLength Infinity)
findings.evidence: Node sorts the rendered entry strings, not the raw keys, and quotes any key that is not /^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*$/. The port sorts raw keys (LogFormat.swift, `members.keys.sorted()`), treats `$` and non-ASCII letters as bare identifiers (inspectKey, `$0 == "$" || $0.properties.isAlphabetic`), and puts no quote character first in the sort. I ran the reference with `node -e 'const {inspect}=require("util");console.log(inspect({a:1,a1:2,"a-b":3,b:4,$x:5},{depth:8,breakLength:Infinity,compact:true,sorted:true}))'`. It prints `{ '$x': 5, 'a-b': 3, a1: 2, a: 1, b: 4 }`. The port's algorithm gives `{ a: 1, a-b: ... }`: raw-key sort gives a, a-b, a1, b, $x. It also writes `$x` unquoted and `a-b` with the wrong quoting or order. Keys such as `a`/`a1` order differently because ':' (0x3a) sorts after digits in the rendered `key: value` strings. The same applies to `$`-prefixed and quoted keys, which sort first because of the leading quote. Writing structured entries (`write(level:namespace:message:context:)`) with such context keys gives a different app.log line than the reference. No test covers this: Tests/FTFileSystemTests/Logging/AppLoggerTests.swift has no `sorted` or inspect-ordering case. Reproduce the port side with a Swift test calling `LogFormat.arguments([.context(["a":.number(1),"a1":.number(2),"$x":.number(5)])])` and comparing to `{ '$x': 5, a1: 2, a: 1 }`.

fixes.summary: Fixed finding 1 in Sources/FTFileSystem/Logging/LogFormat.swift. Object entries are now rendered as `key: value` strings and sorted by UTF-16 code unit, as Node does. Keys are bare only if they match /^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*$/, so `$x`, `a-b` and non-ASCII keys are quoted. I added a test, `contextEntriesSortAsRenderedStringsAndQuoteNonIdentifierKeys`, to Tests/FTFileSystemTests/Logging/AppLoggerTests.swift. Its expected strings were checked against real `util.inspect` output. It covers `{ '$x': 5, 'a-b': 3, 'é': 6, a1: 2, a: 1, b: 4 }` and the `{ '$x': 5, a1: 2, a: 1 }` case from the review. I did not run the test against the old code before fixing, so the failing-first step was skipped. I also corrected the expected string in `aLineIsTheISOTimeTheLevelAndTheArguments`, which had the old raw-key order. `scripts/ci.sh` passes (build, test, format). The commit carries the Port-Stage: fixed-1 trailer, and the worktree is detached. Quiet mode was respected: nothing was launched or shown on screen.

P0-13.title: W1-E follow-ups: flaky eject/thumbnail tests, listing bench metrics
P0-13.summary:
Causes found and fixed in tests only. Thumbnail tests (ThumbnailStoreTests, ThumbnailLoadQueueTests) used fixed yields plus a 150 ms sleep, so they raced main-actor tasks under load; they now wait on queue idle or the expected call count. DiskImage.withVolume now holds a per-kind flock, because parallel clones of one blank image share a UUID and the second attach failed with "no mountable file systems"; detach wait raised to 30 s. Listing bench: tools/bench/run.sh runs listing.sh, report.py reads build/bench/listing.json, budgets.json gains list_3000_ms (25) and list_100000_ms (400); listing.sh gave 7.6 ms and 280 ms.
Failure rates (full swift test under CPU load): before, 1 in 4 at 12 spinners (thumbnail), 1 in 8 at 16 spinners (DiskImageSelfTests attach); after, 0 in 8 at 8 spinners. The 16-spinner run after the fix still failed 3 in 10, in other suites' timing tests, one forced-eject EBUSY, and one attach failure before the detach timeout was raised. Unloaded, the gate loop passed 8 of 8 both before and after, and scripts/ci.sh passed. The eject flake itself did not reproduce unloaded, and the forced-eject EBUSY on DADiskEject under extreme load is unresolved.

fixes.summary:
Fixed at 56ae0deed1174953dbc646ef868a9763280181fa on port/P0-13. The intermittent failure never reproduced for me, so the cause is inferred and the new test is not a failing-first test. Both gates pass: 8 filtered iterations, then scripts/ci.sh (940 tests, 0 failures). I also ran scripts/ci.sh six times beforehand with no failure.

Likely cause: the test checked `!isMounted(folder.path)`, a mount-path check. Between the eject and that check, another process can attach a clone of the same blank image and take the freed `/Volumes/<name>`. Candidates are another worktree's test run on older code without the cross-process lock, or ExecPlaces' unlocked attaches. The path then shows mounted even though our volume is gone.

The fix is in `Tests/FTFileSystemTests/Volumes/VolumeEjectorTests.swift`. The tests now record the volume's device node (`/dev/diskNsM`) before ejecting and assert that device is no longer mounted. The same change applies to the other three eject tests that checked the path.

Earlier commits on the branch already cover the thumbnail flakiness, the per-kind disk-image `flock`, and the listing bench metrics.
remaining: Did not reproduce the failure, so the cause above is not confirmed, and I have no before/after failure rates under a parallel `swift build` load.

ExecDiskImages in `Tests/FTTestSupport/ExecPlaces.swift` still attaches clones of the same blank images without the per-kind lock. It holds them until process exit, so locking it would hang `DiskImage.withVolume`. If the flake returns, look there first.

deviations: The eject-test flake was not reproduced at realistic load; the fix targets the disk-image attach race seen in DiskImageSelfTests, which shares the helper with VolumeEjectorTests.

At 16 CPU spinners, VolumeEjectorTests' forced eject once failed with EBUSY from DADiskEject on the whole disk after a forced unmount; left unfixed since it only appears under extreme load and mirrors the original's behavior.
Timing-budget tests in other suites (WriteEffectsTests, ResponseCacheTests, CommandAvailabilityTests) fail under 12 to 16 CPU spinners; not in this package's ownership.
